answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable stake and earn trust through audited, useful work before it can influence allocation. A Sybil attacker must fund many separate deposits and keep them tied up, making mass identities costly; colluding agents can still pass work between one another, so random independent audits and stake slashing help but cannot prove honesty. Even a relic discovered on a voyage and recorded with a quill needs verification.
